GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
DEPARTMENT OF ECONOMIC AFFAIRS 
 
LOK SABHA  
UN-STARRED QUESTION NO.: 3979 
 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 28TH MARCH, 2022/ 7 CHAITRA, 1944 (SAKA) 
 
IRREGULARITIES IN NSE 
 
3979. SHRI DAYANIDHI MARAN 
          SHRI MANISH TEWARI 
          SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS LALAN SINGH 
          SHRI S. VENKATESAN 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that former National Stock Exchange (NSE) Managing Director allegedly 
abused the server architecture  of the Exchange to provide biased and quicker access to a 
private company and quantum of the data illegally shared; 
(b) if so, the details thereof along with name of the private company that was allegedly favored; 
(c) whether the case was registered in 2018 and yet the investigation is being conducted only now 
in 2022 and if so, the reasons for the delay;  
(d) whether it is a fact that this fraud was caused by installation of a small device and if so, whether 
the security measures at the NSE are lax and su sceptible to such and bigger threats like a 
cyber-attack in the future; 
(e) if so, whether any steps have been taken to harden the security of the trading platforms and if 
so, the details thereof along with the details of cyber- security teams engaged to identify and 
trace the leak of sensitive information including the people involved; 
(f) the details of other actions taken by the Government/ SEBI in the irregularities found in NSE 
and against those found involved therein; and  
(g) whether lot of foreign exchange involved in NSE and RBI roll is to be reviewed to avoid any 
such frauds in future and if so, the details thereof along with other measures taken in this 
regard? 
 
ANSWER 
SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHRY 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR FINANCE 
 
(a) and (b):  SEBI received certain complaints in the year 2015 alleging certai n irregularities in 
respect of c o-location facility provided by NSE.  On examination/investigation by SEBI, it was 
noticed that due to lack of sufficient checks in the system architecture, a few stock brokers connected 
to the exchange market data feed system through secondary server and had latency advantage. For 
lapses in this regard, NSE’s former MD and CEOs have been held responsible for breaches of the 
relevant provisions of Securities Contracts (Regulations) (Stock Exchanges and Clearing 
Corporations) Regulations, 2012. Further, SEBI  passed various order against M/s OPG Securities 

Private Limited and initiated adjudication proceedings against various entities in the matter of 
preferential access to Tick-By-Tick (TBT) data feed to certain trading members. 
 (c): CBI has registered a cas e in the year 2018 under sections 120 -B, 204 Indian Penal Code  & 
Sections 7, 12, 13(2) read with 13(1)(d) of Prevention of Corruption Act , 1988 and Section 66 of 
Information Technology Act, 2000. CBI has informed that substantial progress has been made in the 
investigation of the case.  
(d) & (e): SEBI did not come across any instance to suggest that fraud was caused by installation of 
a small device. Co-location issue at NSE was caused by NSE not exercising the requisite due diligence 
while putting in place the TBT market data feed dissemination architecture.  
(f): SEBI after thorough examination initiated proceedings against NSE and othe r entities and 
consequently passed orders in the matter of NSE Colocatio n TBT data, NSE -Dark Fibre and NSE 
corporate governance. Further, Income Tax Department has conducted investigations to unearth the 
evasion of tax in case of a few individuals and entities who were alleged to be involved in the 
irregularities found in NSE. However, disclosure of inform  ation about specific cases is prohibited 
except as provided under Section 138 of the Income Tax Act, 1961. 
(g): Allegations in the co-location matter are in the nature of preferential access provided to certain 
trading members and not of involvement of foreign exchange.

TO BE ANSWERED ON MONDAY THE 28TH MARCH, 2022 
CHAITRA 7, 1944 (SAKA) 
TAX ON RAW MATERIALS OF SANITARY NAPKINS 
 
3981. SHRIMATI  APARAJITA SARANGI: 
 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government plans to review and remove any taxation currently levied on the 
raw materials required for production of sanitary napkins and if not, the reasons therefor;  
 
(b)  whether the Government has plans to remove taxation on other essential menstrual hygiene 
products such as tampons, menstrual cups, menstrual cloth, and like -products and if so, the 
reasons therefor; 
 
(c) whether the Government plans to subsidise pan -India menstrual hygiene products and if so, 
the reasons therefor; and 
 
(d whether tax-exemption from GST has led to a reduction in the selling price of sanitary pads 
and tampons and if so, the details thereof? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) and  (b):  GST rates are fixed based on the recommendations of the GST Council. The GST 
rate for ‘Sanitary towels (pads) or sanitary napkins; tampons’ as prescribed by the GST Council 
is ‘Nil’ with effect from 26.07.2018. As regards raw materials required for production of sanitary 
napkin, at present there is no recommendation of the GST Council for reduction in GST rates on 
such raw materials. 
(c):  The Scheme for Promotion of Menstrual Hygiene among adolescent girls in the age group  
of 10-19 years is being implemented by the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare since 2011. 
Since 2015-16, the said scheme is being supported under the National Health Mission through 
the route of State Programme Implementation Plans (PIP), based on the pr oposals received 
from the States/UTs. Under this scheme the sanitary napkins are sold to the adolescent girls at 
a subsidized rate of Rs. 6 for a pack of 6 napkins within the community by the Accredited Social 
Health Activist (ASHA) 
(d):  Since GST is charged as per the specified rate on the value of the supply, any reduction in 
the rate of GST should generally result in a reduction in the final prices. However price of 
production also depends on other cost elements and factors; it may not be feasible to ex actly 
assess the impact of GST reduction on prices.

National Action Plan on Climate Change 
 
3982.  SHRI NARANBHAI KACHHADIYA:  
SHRI BALUBHAU ALIAS SURESH NARAYAN DHANORKAR:  
SHRI MAGUNTA SREENIVASULU REDDY:  
SHRI PARBATBHAI SAVABHAI PATEL:  
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to 
state:  
 
(a)  the objectives of National Action Plan on climate change (NAPCC) and the number of 
parts the said plan has been divided into;  
(b)  whether the poor and weaker sections of the society are likely to be protected from the 
damage caused by climate change through said plan;  
(c)  if so, the action plan prepared in the State of Gujarat to avoid damage caused by 
climate change;  
(d)  whether the Government has taken measures to include carbon emissions under 
National Action Plan for climate change; and  
(e)  whether the Government has taken into account the effects on the livelihood of coal 
workers when moving towards the goal of net-zero emission? 
 
 
A N S W E R 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
( S H R I  A S H W I N I  K U M A R  C H O U B E Y )  
 
(a) to (d)  The National Action Plan on climate change (NAPCC) encompasses eight 
missions in the specific areas of Solar Energy, Enhanced Energy Efficiency, Sustainable 
Habitat, Water, Sustaining the Himalayan Eco-system, Strategic Knowledge for Climate 
Change, Green India, and Sustainable Agriculture. These specific areas tackle core issues 
pertaining to climate change, outlining steps to simultaneously advance India’s development 
and climate change related-objectives of adaptation and mitigation. NAPCC is guided by the 
principles - (i) protecting the poor and vulnerable sections of society through an inclusive and 
sustainable development strategy, sensitive to climate change; (ii) achieving national growth 
through ecological sustainability (iii) devising efficient and cost-effective strategies for end 
use Demand Side Management (iv) deploying appropriate technologies for both adaptation 
and mitigation of greenhouse gases emissions (v) engineering new and innovative forms of 
market, regulatory and voluntary mechanisms to promote sustainable development (vi) 
effecting implementation of programmes by including civil society and local government 
institutions and through public-private partnership; and (vii) welcoming international 
cooperation for research, development, sharing and transfer of technologies. Under the 

 
 
NAPCC Government has initiated several activities, schemes, programmes under the national 
Missions. The activities in the areas of solar energy, energy efficiency and forestry sector are 
linked with reduction in carbon emissions. Other Missions also support carbon emissions 
reduction as co-benefit.  
 
Consistent with the approach of NAPCC, State Action Plans on Climate Change (SAPCCs) 
are already in place for 33 States and Union Territories of the country, including the State of 
Gujarat. States and Union Territories have indicated their sector specific and cross sectoral 
priority actions for combating climate change in its SAPCC. Gujarat’s SAPCC has identified 
priority areas for the State like water, agriculture, health, forests and biodiversity, coastal 
regions, infrastructure, energy efficiency and renewable energy, transport, waste, urban 
development and rural livelihood.  
 
(e) The share of coal in the energy basket is going to remain significant in years ahead, 
while there is push for renewable/non-fossil based energy.

Will the Minister of CULTURE be pleased to state:  
a) whether the Government has  taken any steps for the promotion of literature in 
Indian languages including Gujarati; 
b) if so, the details thereof; 
c) the schemes for young writers, poets in Indian languages; and 
d) the number of youths benefited therefrom, State/UT-wise? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF CULTURE, TOURISM & DEVELOPMENT OF  
NORTH EASTERN REGION 
(G.KISHAN REDDY) 
a&b) Yes Madam. The Government of India has taken a number of steps for the 
promotion of literature in Indian languages including Gujrati. 
 
Sahitya Akademi (an autonomous organizatio n under M/o Culture) promotes 
literature and literary activities in 24 Indian languages. The Akademi publishes

the Akademi holds at least 30 seminars, 200 literary gatherings,  workshops and

For the promotion of Gujarati Literature, there is an Advisory Board of eminent 
writers and scholars in Gujarati to orient the Akademi on publications, translations 
and literary programmes. As per the directions of the Advisory Board members, 
Sahitya Akademi organizes literary progammes in Gujarati. The Akademi brings 
out significant publications of Indian language s and translates them into Gujrati 
language and vice-versa. 

 
c)  In 2011, the Government of India had constituted Sahitya Akademi Yuva Puraskar 
for 24 Indian languages. The Akademi  also conducts Young Writers' Meet. It 
organises programmes titled YuvaSahiti and Avishkar to encourage young writers 
writing in different Indian languages. It also provides travel grant to young 
writers (age 40 or below) under which a writer is offered to take a travel to a 
State other than his/her own to get acquainted with lite rary ambience of another 
language. Besides this, Akademi constituted a publication scheme titled Navodaya 
which undertakes publication of the first literary work of art of the writer. 
 
d)  The Akademi invites writers -scholars on the basis of their contribution to their 
respective languages instead of states they belong to . The language wise list of

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 3984 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 28.03.2022 
 
Amendmnet in Biological Diversity Act, 2002 
 
3984. SHRI MANICKAM  TAGORE  B.:  
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a)  whether it is a fact that the environmentalists have expressed concern over amendments to 
the Biological Diversity Act, 2002 as it prioritizes intellectual property and commercial 
trade at the cost of the Act’s key aim of conserving biological resources; 
(b)  whether it is a fact that the Bill will undo all the efforts made in the last few years to 
implement the Biological Diversity Act; 
(c)  whether the changes do not increase the stake of local communities in sustainable growth; 
and  
(d)  whether it is also true that the amended Bill will benefit the traditional medicine 
manufacturers, seed sector and industry and researchers and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE 
CHANGE  
(SHRI ASHWINI KUMAR CHOUBEY) 
 
(a) to (d) The proposed amendments to the Biological Diversity Act, 2002 aim to enable 
fast-tracking of research, patent application process, transfer of research results 
while utilising the biological resources available in India. Therefore, the efforts 
towards the implementation of the Biological Diversity Act, would remain intact 
and even more effective, including further strengthening the Biodiversity 
Management Committees (BMCs) as communities would continue to get benefits 
through the provisions of Access and Benefit Sharing. The amendments provide 
exemption to seed companies or farmers who have an approval or a right granted 
under the Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers Rights Act, 2001. 
 
For IPR and research activities, only registration process has been introduced for 
Indian controlled entities, to make the process simpler. However, when these 
entities go in for commercialization, they will have to seek approval from 
NBA/SBB, as the case may be.

in the country, if so, the details thereof; 
(b)whether the Government has also formulated any scheme to integrate

MINISTRY OF TOURISM

ANSWERED ON 28.03.2022 
 
INFRASTRUCTURAL DEVELOPMENT PROJECTS IN STATES UNDER SDS   
 
3988.   SHRI RAJBAHADUR SINGH:  
SHRI MANOJ TIWARI:  
SHRI PRATAP CHANDRA SARANGI:  
SHRI BRIJBHUSHAN SHARAN SINGH:  
SHRI SANGAM LAL GUPTA:  
 
Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to state: 
 
 (a)  the key objectives and features of the Swadesh Darshan scheme 
(SDS) along with the details of sanctioned projects under Eco 
Theme under SDS;  
(b)  the Detailed Project Report (DPR) for major ongoing infrastructural 
development projects in the State of Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, 
Uttar Pradesh and NCT of Delhi;  
(c)  the details of funds allocated for the said States under SDS 
towards strengthening Tourism infr astructure through various 
spiritual circuits; and  
(d) the details of Foreign Exchange Earnings (FEEs), in US$ from 
Tourism in the said States during the last three years and the 
current year? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF TOURISM                   (SHRI G. KISHAN REDDY) 
 
(a) to (d): The major objective of the ‘Swadesh Darshan’ scheme 
includes development of circuits with tourist potential in a planned and 
prioritized manner, promote cultural value of the country to generate 
livelihoods in the identified regions, enhancing the tourist attractiveness 
in a sustainable manner by developing world class infrastructure etc.   

 
 
The Ministry of Tourism under  its schemes of  ‘Swadesh Darshan’ 
and ‘National Mission on Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and Spiritual, Heritage 
Augmentation Drive (PRASHAD)’ provides financial assistance to State 
Governments/Union Territory (UT) Administrations/Central Agencies etc. 
for development of tourism infrastructure in the country. The projects  
under these schemes are sanctioned subject to availabilit y of funds, 
submission of suitable Detailed Project Reports (DPR), adherence to 
scheme guidelines and utilization of funds released earlier etc. The  
details of the projects  sanctioned  in the country  under  PRASHAD  
scheme and  various themes  including   eco and spiritual themes in  
Swadesh Darshan  scheme is  at  annexure  I. 
 
The Ministry of  Tourism has  not  sanctioned  any  project  in  Delhi  
under  Swadesh Darshan and  PRASHAD  schemes  however the details 
of the projects  sanctioned  in  Madhya P radesh, Odisha  and  Uttar 
Pradesh is at  annexure  II.  
 
The Ministry of Tourism do not maintain State –wise Foreign 
Exchange Earnings (FEEs). However, the details of Foreign Exchange 
Earnings (FEEs), in US$ from Tourism in the country from 2017 to 2020 is 
at Annexure- III.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION  
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION & LITERACY 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3989 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 28.03.2022 
 
 Education for Children with Special Needs 
 
 
3989. SHRI JAYANT SINHA: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of different aspects under the Inclusive Education for Children with Special Needs 
programme; 
 (b) the number of beneficiaries and the achievements of the programme since its inception, 
State-wise; and 
(c) whether the Government conducts training for teachers and instructors to sensitise them to the 
needs of children with special needs and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRIMATI ANNPURNA DEVI) 
 
(a) The Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Samagra  Shiksha launched in 2018-19, has dedicated 
Inclusive Education component for the education of Children with Special Needs (CwSN) . It 
aims to look at education of CwSN in a continuum from Pre -Nursery to Class XII. The 
scheme covers all children with special needs with one or more disabilities as mentioned in 
the schedule of disabilities of the Rights of the Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016 
studying in Governme nt, Government -aided and local body schools. The objectives of 
Inclusive Education (IE) under Samagra Shiksha are as under: 
 To enable all children and young persons with disabilities to have access to inclusive 
education and improve their enrolment, retent ion and achievement in the general 
education system.  
 Identification of children with disabilities at the school level and assessment of her/his 
educational needs. 

 Provision of aids and appliance and assistive devices, to the children with special needs 
as per requirement. 
 Removal of architectural barriers in schools so that students with disability have access to 
classrooms, laboratories, libraries and toilets in the school. 
 Supplying appropriate teaching learning materials, medical facilities, vocational training 
support, guidance and counselling services and therapeutic services to children with 
special needs as per their requirement in convergence with line departments.  
 General school teachers will be sensitized and trained to teach and involve children  with 
special needs in the general classroom. For existing special educators, capacity building 
programmes will be undertaken.  
 CWSN will have access to support services through special educators, establishment of 
resource rooms, vocational education, therapeutic services and counselling. 
(b) The total enrolment of CWSN in Government and Government Aided Schools covered under 
IE component in the year 2018 -19 and 2019 -20 are 2111497 and 2249127 respectively. The 
statement indicating State/ UT -wise details of total enrolment of CWSN in Government and 
Government Aided Schools in the year 2018-19 and 2019-20 is at Annexure I. 
 
 A statement indicating the activity wise funds allocated  under IE component of Samagra  
Shiksha for the year 2018-19 and 2019-20, as per Prabandh Portal is at Annexure II.  
(c) Yes Sir. Through “NISHTHA” (National Initiative for School Heads and Teachers Holistic 
Advancement), teachers have been imparted training on Inclusive Education module , an integral 
part of NISHTHA training. The statement indicating State/ UT-wise details of teachers who have 
been imparted training on Inclusive Education module in the year 2018 -19 and 2019 -20 is at 
Annexure III.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3990 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 28.03.2022 
 
Indian Institutes of Technology  
 
3990. SHRI SUMEDHANAND SARASWATI: 
  SHRIMATI RANJEETA KOLI: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the new Indian Institute s of Technolog y, established during 
2008-09, have fallen short on all parameters including performance, 
administration, infrastructure etc. 
 
(b) if so, the details thereof alongwith the reasons therefor; and 
 
(c) the corrective steps taken or proposed to be taken by the Government in  
 this regard? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
 
(DR. SUBHAS SARKAR) 
 
(a) to (c ): The establishment of eight new Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs) 
at Ropar, Patna, Hyderabad, Jodhpur, Gandhinagar, Bhubaneswar, Indore and 
Mandi during 2008 -09 faced time and cost overruns primarily due to delay in 
identification, selection and transfer of the land by the respective State 
Governments. Other factors which contributed to delay in infrastructure 
development include grant of various clearances by respective State/local 
authorities, change of approved project cost as per revised CPWD rates, 
exclusion of critical cost components like site specific expenditures, Covid -19 
pandemic situation resulting in less availability of material and labour due to 
restricted mobility, etc. All these IITs are functioning from their permanent 
campus. The progress  was reviewed regularly by the Government and also by 
the concerned IIT in their Building and Works Committee, Finance Committee 
and Board of Governors.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3991 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 28.03.2022 
 
PAYMENT OF GRATUITY 
 
3991. DR. VISHNU PRASAD M.K.:  
 
 Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a)whether the Government has received any representations for 
issuance of notification to provide gratuity up to Rs.20 lakh to the 
employees for the intervening period from January 2016 to March 
2018; 
(b)if so, the details thereof;  
(c)whether Government would consi der taking necessary action for 
issuing the said notification, as very few employees were left out with 
the financial burden not much and employers ready to make payment 
of enhanced gratuity; and 
(d)if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SHRI RAMESWAR TELI) 
 
(a) to (d): The Payment of Gratuity (Amendment) Act, 2018 was passed 
by the Parliament on 28.03.2018 enhancing the gratuity ceiling under the 
Act from ₹10 lakh to ₹20 lakh with effect from 29.03.2018.  
  
Representations have been received from public 
representatives/associations/individuals asking for providing benefits of 
enhanced gratuity under the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 to give 
retrospective effect for enhancing the said ceiling.  
 
   For enhancing the ceiling on gratuity, the Payment of Gratuity 
Act, 1972 was required to be amended every time. However, the Payment 
of Gratuity Act, 1972 had been amended in 2018 empowering the Central 
Government to enhance the ceilings by notification, instead of amen ding 
the said Act, so that the limit can be revised from time to time as per felt 
need. 
******

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA  
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION    
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
 
LOK SABHA  
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3992 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 28.03.2022 
 
Reservation for OBC Students in Hostels 
 
3992. SHRI MARGANI BHARAT: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the reservation is being followed in all Central Universities as per the 
provisions of the Constitution and if so, the details thereof;  
 
(b) whether the Delhi University (DU) is also a Central University; 
 
(c) if so, whether DU is not following reservation for OBC students in hostels; 
 
(d) if so, the details thereof and the reasons therefor; 
 
(e) whether the scholarship is also not being provided to OBC students in DU; and  
 
(f) if  so, the details thereof and the reasons therefor along with the action taken or 
proposed to be taken by the Government against concerned officials in this regard? 
 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUBHAS SARKAR) 
 
(a) to (f) The reservation policy of Govt. of India is followed by all the Central 
Universities except in minority institutions under Article 30(1) of the C onstitution. 
University of Delhi, a Central University, follows the reservation policy for admission in 
various hostels of the University. The implementation of OBC reservation was limited in 
old hostels due to a judgement of Hon’ble Supreme Court of India which necessitated 
implementation of reservation in the Central Educational Institutions ( CEIs) be made in 
accordance with the expansion of capacity to ensure that seats available in unreserved 
category are not reduced. University of Delhi follows the reservation policy for award of 
UGC Non-NET Fellowship to SC, ST and OBC students.

States Report on Forest 
 
3993. DR. T. SUMATHY (a) THAMIZHACHITHANGAPANDIAN: 
SHRI RAKESH SINGH:

Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the Government has expressed concern over poor 
implementation of the compensatory afforestation scheme especially in terms of 
efforts from States/UTs to upload correct information on the portal; 
(b) whether a note submitted by the Forest Survey of India to the Ministry of 
Environment, Forest and Climate Change in January 2020 indicated that only a 
quarter of the data provided by States on plantations was correct, if so, the details 
thereof and the reasons therefor;  
(c) if so, proportion of correct data provided by State Governments on afforestation taken 
up, State-wise particularly in the North East Region; 
(d) whether non-forest areas have also been included in the said reports/maps and forest 
area has been shown as increased and if so, the details thereof and the reasons 
therefor; 
(e) the details of public funds spent on compensatory afforestation, year-wise during the 
last three years and the current year; and 
(f) whether the Government is taking any steps to ensure transparency in compensatory 
afforestation, if so details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI ASHWINI KUMAR CHOUBEY) 
 
(a) to(f) The Compensatory Afforestation Fund (CAMPA fund) are being utilized by 
States/UTs for compensating the loss of forest & tree cover and ecological services 
due to diversion of forest land for various developmental projects through 
compensatory afforestation, activities undercatchment area treatment plan as well 
asfor protection of forests, biodiversity and wildlifeas per approved Annual Plan of 
Operations under the provisions ofCompensatory Afforestation Fund Act, 2016 and 
Rules made thereunder.Compensatory Afforestation and other activities under 
CAMPA Funds are being regularly monitored by the State/UT Forest Departments

wing, and by independent third party agencies. Monitoring reports are being

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
DEPARTMENT OF ECONOMIC AFFAIRS 
 
LOK SABHA UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3994 
 
TO BE ANSWERED ON MONDAY, 28th MARCH, 2022/ CHAITRA 7, 1944   
 
Repatriation of Pension Income 
 
3994. SHRI SANJAY JADHAV:  
 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether it is mandatory for a person, being an individual, to repatriate the 
pension income earned from United Nations outside India in a Bank Account 
maintained with country outside India, when the i ndividual was employed outside 
India; and  
 
(b) if so, the details thereof including the time within which it is to be repatriated? 
 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
  
(a) & (b)  In general, a  person resident in India to whom any amount of foreign 
exchange is due or has accrued is duty bound to take all reasonable steps to realise 
and repatriate such foreign exchange to India, save as otherwise provided under the 
provisions of Foreign Exchange Management Act, (FEMA) , or the rules and                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
regulations made thereunder, or with the general or special permission of the Reserve 
Bank.  
 
However, Section 6(4) of Foreign Exchange Management Act, (FEMA), 1999 permits a 
person resident in India to hold, own, transfer or invest in foreign currency, foreign 
security or any immovable property situated outside India if such currency, security or 
property was acquired, held or owned by such person when he was resident outside 
India or inherited from a person who was resident outside India.  
 
Foreign Exchange Management (Realisatio n, repatriation and surrender of foreign 
exchange) Regulations, 2015  prescribe the manner of repatriation and timeline for 
surrender of foreign exchange.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF TOURISM 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3995 
ANSWERED ON 28.03.2022 
 
NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF WATER SPORTS 
 
3995. SHRI MANOJ KOTAK: 
          SHRIMATI RAKSHA NIKHIL KHADSE: 
 
 Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether it is a fact that there is only institute in the country 
functioning in Goa for training and certification in water sports 
and related activities; 
(b) if so, the details thereof including the details of prerequisites 
for establishment of National Inst itute of Water Sports in 
States in the country; 
(c) whether the Government has any plan to set up National 
Institute of Water Sports in Maharashtra; 
(d) if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) whether the Government is planning to promote the water 
sports in the country a nd if so, the action taken in this 
regards? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTRY OF TOURISM              (SHRI G. KISHAN REDDY) 
 
(a) to (d): National Institute of Water Sports (NIWS), Goa is a 
centre functioning under the Indian Institute of Tourism & Travel 
Management (IITTM), a central autonomous body under the Ministry 
of Tourism, for training and certification in water sports and related 
activities. NIWS, Goa is mandated to impart training in water related 
sports activities across all States and UTs. For opening of any 
centre of a central autonomous body there are factors including 
potential for tourism development, resource availability, viability, 
demand and other such factors and comparative advantage among 

various sites across States and UTs.  No proposal has been 
received in the Ministry for setting up of NIWS in Maharashtra.  
 
(e): The Ministry has been taking concerted efforts to support the 
State and UT Govts. for the promotion of Watersports related 
tourism in the Country.  M inistry of Tourism  provides Grant -in-aid 
support to the State and UT Govts. for the Island, Beach and Water -
front development under the Swadesh Darshan Scheme, to which, 
Watersports, Beach Safety etc. are important components. In 
addition, the Ministry has a mechanism for the approval of 
adventure tour operators in India. 
 
Through the National Institute of Watersports (NIWS) Goa, 
support is provided to the State and UT Governments in matters 
related to preparation of Policies, Guidelines, SOP’s, manpower 
training etc.  To strengthen the activities, NIWS has already entered 
MOU arrangements with State and UT Governments as well as the 
Indian Navy Physical Training School.   
 
Over 27 courses in Watersports and related activities have 
also been developed by NIWS. The trainers of the Institute also 
imparts training to different States and UT’s and undertake off -
campus training courses. NIWS also undertakes watersports 
awareness campaigns on both online and physical modes.

RESTORATION AND PRESERVATION OF OLDEST FLAG 
 
 
3996.  SHRI THIRUNAVUKKARASAR SU: 
 
 
 Will the Minister of CULTURE be pleased to state: 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
(a) whether the oldest National Flag hoisted on August 15, 1947 is lying  
in a dilapidated condition; 
(b) if so, whether the  Archaeological Survey of India ( ASI) has set up an Expert 
Committee for its  restoration and preservation and the estimated cost of the  
project; 
(c) if so, the details thereof; and 
  
(d) the time by which the project is likely to be completed? 
 
MINISTER OF CULTURE, TOURISM AND DEVELOPMENT OF NORTH EASTERN REGION 
(SHRI G. KISHAN REDDY) 
(a) 
to 
(d) 
The oldest National Flag hoisted on August 15, 1947 is in St. George Fort, 
Chennai and is in a delicate condition.   Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) has 
set up an expert committee for restoration and preservation of the National F lag. 
Estimated cost of the project is Rs.13 Lakhs. 
 
The scientific studies have been carried out by the ASI with the help of Textile 
Committee, Chennai, Govt. of India, Ministry of Textiles and Indira Gandhi Centre 
for Atomic Research (IGCAR), Kalpakkam using non destructive t echniques prior 
to start of conservation of the National F lag. Complete photo and video 
documentation has also been done.   On the basis of scientific studie s and 
suggestions of the expert  committee, the conservation and preservation work is 
being carried out so as to complete the project at the earliest.

Green Belt Areas 
 
3997.SHRI NAYAB SINGH:  
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGEbe pleased to 
state: 
(a) the initiative being taken by the Government for insuring larger green belt areas in 
urban areas under the Public-Private Partnership (PPP) mode; 
(b) whether the Government has identified newly developed green belt areas in rural and 
urban areas of the country; and  
(c) if so, the details thereof, State-wise including Haryana? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE 
CHANGE  
(SHRI ASHWINI KUMAR CHOUBEY) 
(a) to(c) The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change supports the States/Union 
Territories for carrying out afforestation activities in both forest and non-forest land 
including Urban and Rural areas under National Mission for a Green India (GIM) and 
CAMPA. Further, afforestation is being carried out by the States/Union Territories 
under various schemes of Central Government and State Government. As per report 
compiled in the Ministry under twenty-point programme, afforestation is being taken 
up annually over 2.0 million ha since 2019-20.Details of fund released/disbursedunder 
GIM and CAMPA including Haryanais enclosed at Annexure-I. 
  In addition, the Ministryhas also launchedNagar Van Yojana (NVY) for providing 
wholesome healthy living environment, and contributingto growth of Smart,

Vans and 200 Nagar Vatikas in the country during the period of 2020-21 to 2024-25 
with an objective to significantly enhance the tree outside forests and green cover, 
enhancement of biodiversity and ecological benefits to the urban and peri-urban areas 
apart from improving quality of life of city dwellers. So far, a total of 65 projects have 
been sanctioned in 22 States including Haryana. The State-wise details of Nagar Van 
projects sanctioned under Nagar Van scheme are given in Annexure-II.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION & LITERACY 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3998 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 28.03.2022 
 
KVs IN ASPIRATIONAL DISTRICTS 
 
3998.  SHRI LAVU SRI KRISHNA DEVARAYALU:  
SHRI POCHA BRAHMANANDA REDDY:  
DR. BEESETTI VENKATA SATYAVATHI:  
SHRI M.V.V. SATYANARAYANA:  
SHRI SANJAY KAKA PATIL:  
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state:  
 
(a)  whether it is true that Kendriya Vidyalayas (KVs) are functioning in 115 
districts of the country and if so, details thereof;  
(b)  whether it is also true that the Government has identified 125 districts as 
Aspirational Districts;  
(c)  if so, whether this indicates that 10 Aspirational Districts do not have KV;  
(d)  if so, whether the Government consider setting up of KVs in the left out 
Aspirational Districts of the country;  
(e)  the details of constraints that the Government has been facing in setting up of 
KVs in the remaining Aspirational Districts;  
(f)  the details of the number of KVs in Guntur district Andhra Pradesh and 
whether the Government is considering setting up more KVs in Andhra 
Pradesh; and  
(g)  if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SMT. ANNPURNA DEVI) 
 
(a)   At present 1244 Kendriya Vidyalayas (KVs) are functioning in 562 districts 
across the country.  
(b) & (c) Niti Aayog has identified 112 districts in the country as Aspirational Districts 
out of which 16 districts do not have any KV. However, there ar e 160 KVs in 96 
Aspirational Districts.  

(d) & (e) Opening of new KVs is a continuous process. KVs are opened primarily to 
cater to the educational needs of the wards of transferable Central Government 
Employees including Defence& Para -Military personnel, Central Autonomous 
Bodies, Central Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) and Central Institute of Higher 
Learning (IHL) by providing a common programme of education throughout the 
country. Proposals for opening of new KVs are considered only if sponsored by 
Ministries or Departments of the Government of India / State Governments / Union 
Territories (UTs) Administrations and committing resources for setting up a new KV. 
The proposals received from various sponsoring authorities found fulfilling the 
mandatory pre-requisites for opening of new KVs have to compete with other such 
proposals under the “Challenge Method” and subject to approval of the competent 
authority. KVs are not opened on the criteria of State/District/ Aspirational District -
wise. 
(f) & (g) At present, 5 KVs namely KV Guntur, KV Surya Lanka (AFS), KV Tenali, KV 
Sattanpali and KV Irlapadu Village are functioning in Guntur district of Andhra 
Pradesh. Four proposals for setting up of new KVs at Anakapalli (Visakhapatnam), 
Macherla (Guntur), Nandigama (Krishna) and Rompicherla (Guntur) in the State of 
Andhra Pradesh have been found fulfilling the mandatory pre -requisite as per norms 
of Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan.  These proposals have been considered by the 
“Challenge Method” Committee.  
*****

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.3999 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 28.03.2022 
  
SKILL HUB INITIATIVE PROGRAMME 
 
3999. SHRI KRIPANATH MALLAH: 
  
Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRE NEURSHIP be 
pleased to state: 
  
(a) whether the Government is proposing to launch S kill Hub Initiative program within 
the country; 
 
(b)  if so, the details thereof; 
 
(c) the details of the estimated amount under this program; 
 
(d) the details of the target set; 
 
(e) whether the Government has planned to cover Ass am under this program; and 
 
(f) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reas ons therefore? 
 
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE 
MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
(SHRI RAJEEV CHANDRASEKHAR) 
 
(a) to (d) Ministry of Skill development and Entrep reneurship (MSDE) in co-ordination 
with Ministry of Education has launched the Skill H ubs Initiative (SHI) as a pilot on 
01.01.2022 under central component of PMKVY 3.0. 
  
SHI aims at creating shared infrastructure, alignin g with the needs of the local 
economy and addressing the needs of all target segm ents for vocational training. It 
focuses on introduction of skill training programme  in the education ecosystem as 
envisioned in the National Education Policy, 2020 ( NEP, 2020).  Skill Hubs are nodal skill 
centres identified to provide skill development and  vocational training opportunities to 
target population segments from class 6 
th  to 8 th  (introduction to world-of-work through 
orientation, industry visits, bag-less days), Class  9 th  to 12 th  (aimed at exposing students to 
skill development avenues), school dropouts, and ou t-of-education (aimed for academic 
credit, mainstreaming back to education and or apprenticeship and employment linkages). 
  
            The estimated outlay of SHI is Rs. 700 crore. As on 23.03.2022, a total target of 
around 9.3 lakh students has been earmarked under S HI. Out of which, 1.56 lakh 
candidates have been enrolled so far. 
  
(e) and (f)       SHI is being implemented in the S tate of Assam. Till 23.03.2022, 22,600 
targets have been allocated in State of Assam. 
  
*****
